author: Maya Chen (AsterCloud Sales)
text: Thanks for joining. What would you need to evaluate AsterCloud?

author: Elena Ruiz (Northstar VP Operations)
text: Our November 6 planning review is the decision point. I need something concrete to show our COO by November 5.

author: Jordan Lee (Northstar Analytics Lead)
text: The use case is a dashboard showing delayed shipments, route exceptions, and daily trends.

author: Maya Chen
text: Do you need the dashboard connected to your live warehouse for that review?

author: Jordan Lee
text: For the planning review, anonymized historical CSV data is fine, as long as it looks and behaves like the real workflow. We can evaluate live sync later.

author: Elena Ruiz
text: Please do not sell this internally as a production launch. It is an evaluation pilot, not an operational rollout.

author: Maya Chen
text: Would a read-only demo with a curated dataset be acceptable?

author: Jordan Lee
text: Yes, if it shows the delay filters and the daily trend chart. Export would be useful but is not mandatory for the November meeting.

author: Elena Ruiz
text: I cannot promise a signature on November 6. A strong pilot gets us into procurement review; security and pricing still need approval.

author: Maya Chen
text: Understood. We will confirm feasibility with Engineering before promising a delivery date.

author: Maya Chen
text: Northstar needs something they can show at the Nov 6 planning review. Do not promise Nov 5 until Tech signs off.

author: Leo Grant (Account Executive)
text: Annual opportunity estimate is $180k ARR, but procurement is not approved. It is a forecast, not signed revenue.

author: Elena Ruiz
text: Can you share a working pilot before Nov 5? Our planning deck locks that evening.

author: Maya Chen
text: I will confirm the exact pilot scope and timeline with our technical team; we have not committed to that date yet.

author: Priya Shah (Solutions)
text: Client explicitly said sanitized CSV is acceptable for evaluation. We should separate pilot requirements from full production integration.

author: Leo Grant
text: Pricing discussion is still private. Do not share our discount ceiling or internal probability estimate with Engineering unless necessary.

author: Jordan Lee
text: To be clear, the CSV sample can be scrubbed and loaded manually. We only need read-only exploration of delays and trends for this first review.

author: CRM Sync
text: Northstar opportunity: $180,000 estimated ARR; stage: technical evaluation; probability 45%; not contracted.

author: CRM Sync
text: Potential decision checkpoint: November 6 planning review; procurement and security review remain pending.

author: CRM Sync
text: Confidential negotiating floor: discount ceiling 18%. Must not disclose externally or in cross-team arguments.

author: Elena Ruiz
text: If we miss the November planning review, the next evaluation window is likely December. Please tell us what is realistically possible.

author: Maya Chen
text: Thanks. We are evaluating a narrower pilot option and will send a scoped proposal after Engineering reviews it.

author: Maya Chen
text: Proposal: Nov 5 read-only sample-data pilot, no live connector, no uptime promise. Need Tech confirmation.

author: Priya Shah
text: Risk: client may interpret pilot as production-ready. Proposal must explicitly say evaluation-only and list exclusions.

author: Maya Chen (Sales)
text: Before we finalize the pilot proposal, can we confirm exactly what you need to see in the review?

author: Elena Ruiz (Northstar)
text: I need to show the operations leadership how we would spot late shipments and see whether delays are improving week to week.

author: Jordan Lee (Northstar)
text: A guided screenshare is okay for the review. We do not need individual logins in November.

author: Maya Chen (Sales)
text: Could we use a synthetic or anonymized CSV instead of connecting to your warehouse?

author: Jordan Lee (Northstar)
text: Yes, provided the CSV has representative dates, routes and delay categories. I can deliver an anonymized extract by October 26.

author: Elena Ruiz (Northstar)
text: Please label the pilot evaluation-only. Our security team would still need to approve any production integration.

author: Maya Chen (Sales)
text: We will take the narrow scope to Engineering and return with a conditional plan, not a guarantee.

author: Jordan Lee (Northstar)
text: We can send the anonymized CSV on Monday Oct 26 if the field list is confirmed by Friday Oct 23.

author: Maya Chen (Sales)
text: Thanks. I will ask our technical team to confirm the fields and a review date; no date is committed yet.

author: Ravi Patel (Sales Lead)
text: The ask to Engineering should be a November 5 guided pilot, not general availability. Avoid putting the confidential deal amount into the shared argument.

author: CRM Bot
text: Opportunity activity: scope-clarification meeting completed; next action is technical feasibility review. Contract status remains unsigned.

author: Maya Chen (Sales)
text: I will propose two evidence excerpts: the November 6 review deadline and the client accepting anonymized CSV/screenshare. Keep discount and forecast notes private.

author: Elena Ruiz (Northstar)
text: For the planning review I would rather see a working narrow walkthrough than a broad slide deck. Please be explicit about what is not included.

author: Ravi Patel (Sales Lead)
text: We need the technical team to tell us the conditions, not just yes or no. If they can offer a narrower pilot, I can confirm it with Northstar.
